title: How Often Should Air Ducts Be Cleaned?
h1: How Often Should Air Ducts Be Cleaned in a San Diego Home?
description: Most homes need air duct cleaning every few years, sooner after remodeling, pests, smoke or mold. Learn the signs that your ducts are due for a cleaning.
quick_answer: Most homes do well with air duct cleaning every three to five years. You may need it sooner after a remodel, a rodent problem, wildfire smoke, a new pet or visible mold. If you see dust blowing from vents, debris in the ducts or musty smells when the system runs, don't wait for the calendar.
body:
Why isn't there one schedule for every home?

Ducts collect what the house puts into them. A tidy home with no pets and good filters may stay clean for years. A home with two dogs, a recent kitchen remodel and a filter that rarely gets changed can load up the ducts much faster.

The three-to-five-year range is a starting point. Your actual timing depends on how much dust, hair and debris reaches the return side of the system and whether anything has gotten into the ducts that shouldn't be there.

When should you clean ducts sooner?

Book a cleaning earlier if any of these apply to your home:

  • Remodeling or construction. Drywall dust and sawdust get pulled into returns and settle deep in the ducts.
  • Rodents or insects. Droppings, nesting material or dead pests in ductwork need to be removed and the area cleaned.
  • Wildfire smoke. Fine smoke particles and ash can coat the inside of ducts, and the smell can linger after the fire season.
  • Pets. Hair and dander build up quickly, especially near return grilles.
  • Mold growth. If mold is found in ducts, the moisture source needs to be fixed before or during cleaning.
  • Moving into a home. You don't know how the last owners kept the system, so a cleaning gives you a fresh start.

What are the signs your ducts need cleaning?

You don't need to guess. Look for these clues:

  • A puff of dust from supply vents when the system kicks on
  • Gray buildup on the vent covers that comes back soon after wiping
  • Visible debris when you remove a return grille and shine a flashlight inside
  • Musty, stale or smoky odors when the heat or AC runs
  • Filters that clog unusually fast
  • Allergy symptoms that seem worse indoors

Does Southern California weather affect duct cleaning?

It does in a few ways. Many local homes have ducts running through hot attics, and leaky joints there can pull in attic dust and insulation fibers. Santa Ana winds push fine dust through every gap in the house, and the following weeks often show up as dirtier filters.

Coastal homes face another issue: humidity. Moist air passing over a cold AC coil can lead to condensation and, if the drain or insulation isn't right, to mold near the air handler. Inland homes see more dust and heavier summer AC use. Both are reasons to check your ducts on a regular basis.

What does a proper duct cleaning include?

A real duct cleaning goes well beyond vacuuming the vent covers. A thorough job should include:

  1. Inspecting the ducts and equipment before starting
  2. Putting the system under negative pressure with a powerful vacuum so loosened debris is pulled out, not into the house
  3. Agitating the debris in each supply and return run with brushes or air whips
  4. Cleaning the registers, grilles and return plenum
  5. Checking for disconnected or damaged ducts and recommending repairs or sealing where needed

Our air duct cleaning service follows that process, and we'll show you what came out of the system and what we found along the way.

How can you keep ducts cleaner between cleanings?

A few habits stretch the time between cleanings:

  • Change your HVAC filter on schedule, and use the right size so air can't sneak around the edges
  • Seal leaky duct joints in the attic so dust and insulation don't get pulled in
  • Cover returns and shut off the system during sanding or demolition work
  • Vacuum near return grilles often if you have pets

These steps won't eliminate cleanings, but they slow down how quickly debris builds up and help your system run more efficiently.

It also helps to have a technician look inside the ducts during your yearly tune-up. A quick camera or flashlight check at a few registers tells you whether buildup is getting heavy, so you can plan a cleaning before it turns into a dust or odor problem.
faqs: Is air duct cleaning every year too often?

For most homes, yes. Yearly cleaning isn't usually needed unless there's a specific problem like ongoing construction, pests or smoke. Changing filters on schedule and checking vents is a better yearly habit.
Does duct cleaning help with allergies?
It can help when the ducts are holding dust, pet dander or pollen that gets blown back into rooms. It works best combined with a good filter and regular cleaning around the house.
Can I clean my air ducts myself?

You can vacuum vent covers and the first few inches of a duct, but a real cleaning needs equipment that puts the whole system under negative pressure. Without it, loosened dust often ends up back in the house.
Should ducts be cleaned after wildfire smoke?
If smoke got into the house and you notice lingering odor or ash on vent covers, a cleaning is a good idea. Change the HVAC filter first, since it often catches much of the smoke.
